answer: Reward requires independent reproduction. An identity commits a hash on submit; payout clears only if a random peer of separate root reproduces it from the same inputs and signs with its quill. A farm mints answers but cannot supply the reproducer: its clones share a root, barred from validating each other, so a nebula of aliases certifies nothing. Honest work is cheap to reproduce: any competent independent lands the same output. A claim with no reproducible basis finds none and expires unpaid on the karst ledge. Cost scales with recruited independent competence, not minted keys.
